newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu to decide on currency reform.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu to decide on currency reform.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will intervene in a dispute between the Bank of Israel and the Treasury to advance a programme of foreign currency liberalisation, government sources said on Tuesday.
The central bank and the Treasury disagree on details of the liberalisation, especially with regard to investments by Israeli provident funds abroad.
Netanyahu will summon central bank Governor Jacob Frenkel and Finance Minister Dan Meridor for a meeting soon to resolve the differences, the sources said. No date has been set for the meeting.
The Bank of Israel would like to lift foreign currency controls over a number of years until the shekel becomes fully convertible.
Among the steps the central bank recommends:
- Allowing provident funds and institutional investors to invest up to five percent of their assets in foreign securities against two percent currently;
- Allowing companies to invest in foreign securities with no limitation; currently they may invest 10 percent of their capital or five percent of their turnover;
- Allowing Israelis to buy dollars freely from banks and open dollar accounts.

Talks on the programme began more than a year ago but were halted two months ago after the central bank rejected the Treasury's proposal to gradually increase the amount provident funds may invest abroad.
The Treasury's proposal sought to control fluctuations in the level of foreign investment at individual funds, which the central bank said was not viable.
